speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you've listed your symptoms, but I need to ask a few specific questions to narrow this down. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or stool color recently, and do you have a history of liver disease? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests; REQUEST TEST: CBC (Complete Blood Count).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Tests: Not Requested; CBC (Complete Blood Count): WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC shows elevated white blood cells and mild anemia, which, combined with your enlarged supraclavicular lymph node, raises concern for a systemic malignancy. Have you experienced any persistent fevers or drenching night sweats in the last month? REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of elevated white blood cells, anemia, weight loss, night sweats, and an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node is highly concerning for leukemia or lymphoma. Given the abdominal pain, have you noticed any specific pain in your upper right or left quadrant, or any palpable masses? REQUEST IMAGES: Review the CT Abdomen and Pelvis results immediately.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma with possible hepatic or splenic involvement. The fixed supraclavicular node, B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), and cytopenias strongly support a malignant lymphoproliferative disorder. I recommend proceeding with a biopsy of the lymph node for definitive histology.
